summary: Iteration 4 backend + frontend tested. Cost parser auto-detection works on both cost_v2.xlsx (Sheet3 header row 0, 2 cols → 30,568 rows parsed) and cost_prod.xlsx (legacy Sheet3 header row 2 with cost+shipping). ASIN mapping endpoints all functional: template CSV streams 2,037 ASINs with correct header, upload inserts/upserts, list+search work case-insensitively, reprocess returns orders_remapped. Frontend Uploads page renders dropzone-asin (.csv,.xlsx), asin-info card with explainer, and download-asin-template button that successfully downloads asin_mapping_template.csv. HOWEVER: discovered a CRITICAL idempotency bug — apply_asin_mapping (server.py line 422) rewrites line_key to {po}::{merchant_sku}, contradicting the spec ('line_key always uses ASIN'). This breaks re-upload idempotency, creates duplicates (DB now has 6,614 Amazon orders vs 6,580 expected = 34 dupes for the test ASIN B00PB8WM4S), and causes orders_remapped to read 0 on subsequent mapping uploads. 6/9 new pytest tests pass; the 3 failing tests all point to the same root-cause line.

critical.issue: apply_asin_mapping (server.py line 422) overwrites line_key from {po}::ASIN to {po}::merchant_sku at upload time. Breaks the spec requirement 'line_key always uses ASIN so re-uploads are idempotent'. Result: (1) every Amazon PO re-upload after a mapping exists creates duplicate rows (34 dup rows now in DB for B00PB8WM4S→SAND_116_15x20_white); (2) /api/orders?marketplaces=Amazon Vendor returns 6,614 instead of 6,580; (3) POST /api/uploads/asin-mapping reports orders_remapped=0 even on first apply, because by the time _remap_amazon_orders runs, sku is already merchant_sku (apply_asin_mapping already rewrote it during prior upload). FIX: delete line 422 entirely; line_key must remain {order_id}::{ASIN} set by parse_amazon_po. Also one-time cleanup: db.orders.delete_many({source:'amazon_po', line_key:{$regex: '::(?!B[0-9A-Z]{9}$)'}}) — i.e. remove rows whose line_key suffix is not an ASIN pattern.

minor.issue: Endpoint accepts only marketplaces/sku/date filters but no source filter — tests had to use marketplaces='Amazon Vendor' to count Amazon PO orders. Consider adding ?source= filter.
Misleading 0 value when mapping was already applied at upload time. Once line_key bug is fixed, this will naturally read >0 on first mapping upload.

_remap_amazon_orders iterates every Amazon order via async for + per-row update_one — N round-trips for ~6,580 rows. Use bulk_write or update_many per (asin, merchant_sku) group.

rca of the issue.bug: Re-uploading Amazon PO after an ASIN mapping is applied creates duplicate orders.
rca of the issue.root_cause: apply_asin_mapping (server.py:413-423) is called from upload_orders right after parse_amazon_po. It rewrites both sku AND line_key (line 422: r['line_key'] = f"{r['order_id']}::{r['sku']}"). Since sku is now the merchant_sku, line_key becomes {po}::{merchant_sku}. But parse_amazon_po set it to {po}::{ASIN} initially, and the unique upsert key db.orders is line_key, so on next upload the new {po}::{ASIN} doesn't match the stored {po}::{merchant_sku} → inserted as new row.
rca of the issue.reproduction: 1) Upload amazon_po.xls (6580 rows, all ASIN-based line_keys). 2) POST /api/uploads/asin-mapping with {B00PB8WM4S, SAND_116_15x20_white} — this triggers _remap which only changes sku, line_keys stay ASIN. 3) Re-upload amazon_po.xls — apply_asin_mapping runs, sees B00PB8WM4S in mapping, rewrites line_key to {po}::SAND_*. 34 new rows inserted. DB now has 6580 ASIN-keyed + 34 SAND-keyed = 6614 amazon orders.
rca of the issue.mitigation: 1) Delete server.py line 422. 2) One-time DB cleanup: db.orders.delete_many({source:'amazon_po', line_key:{$not:{$regex:'::B[0-9A-Z]{9}$'}}}). 3) Re-run pytest — should be 9/9 pass.
